All Subdivisions hereafter established shall be developed in accordance with the minimum. design standards set forth in this Ordinance.

Suitability of Land. Land subject to flooding, improper drainage, or erosion, or which is for topographical, geological or other reasons unsuitable for residential use shall not be platted for residential use nor for any other uses that will continue to increase the danger to the health, safety, or property destruction, unless the hazards can be and are corrected. Determination will be made by a study of topographic maps, inspecting of the subdivision and/or discussion at a regular Town of Clermont Council (hereafter “Town Council”)

meeting.

Name of Subdivision. The name of the subdivision must have the approval of the Town Council. The name shall not duplicate nor closely approximate the name of an existing subdivision in Hall County.

Lot Size. One (1) acre density with a minimum of three quarter (3/4) of an acre lots, 32,670 square feet.

Covenants. All covenants proposed by the landowner and/or developer of a subdivision shall be submitted in writing to the Clermont Town Council which must give final approval before said covenants can be recorded. The Town Council may use District restrictions as a guideline for accepting covenants,

Access. Access to every subdivision lot shall be provided over a public street.

Through Traffic. Minor streets shall be laid out that their use by through traffic will be discouraged.

Continuation of Existing Street Patterns. Whenever topography, ownership, and design objectives will permit, the street pattern within a Subdivision shall provide for the continuation of appropriate projection of the existing street pattern in the section of the town involved.

Prior to submission to the Town Council, an independent engineer shall be hired by the Town Council to inspect and approval all Subdivision plans, with all fees and costs associated with the inspection to be paid by developer.

Continuation of Existing Streets. Existing streets shall be continued at the same width as the existing street, provided however, that the existing street shall have a right-of-way of at least 30 feet. In no case shall the width of the new street be less than the width of the existing street.

Connections with Future Subdivision. Streets may be reserved at strategic locations to provide for future access to adjoining properties which may be subdivided in the future. Each street connection shall interest property lines at a ninety (90) degree angle if streets are reserved.

Street Names. Street names shall require the approval of the Town Council. Streets that are obviously in alignment with streets already in existence and already named shall be given the name of the existing street. Names of the new streets shall not duplicate or closely approximate those of existing streets in the town. |

Development Along Major Streets, Limited Access Highways. Where a subdivision abuts or contains an expressway, freeway, arterial or collector street, the Town Council may require a street approximately parallel to and on each side of such right-of-way either as a marginal access street, or at a distance suitable for an appropriate use of intervening land, with a non-access reservation suitably planted. Due regard should be given requirements for approach grades and future grade separations in determining distances. Lots shall have no access to expressways, freeways, or arterial streets, but only to an accessible street in which case the Town Council may require double frontage lots.

Any planned one way street shall be clearly shown on the development plat.

Design Requirements.

Street jobs, or centerline off-sets in the horizontal alignment of streets across intersections of less than 200 feet shall be prohibited.

Street Intersections. Whenever feasible, streets shall be laid out so as to intersect as nearly as possible to right angles.

Access. The network of streets within a subdivision must, at some point, access a publicly maintained road or street.

Dams. Any road in which a section crosses over a dam shall be designed as a separate road and shall not be accepted into the Town street system. No street shall be designed or constructed below any dam within the breach floodway of the dam. All dams must be approved by the Department of Natural Resources in accordance with the “Safe Dam Act.”

Property Line Radius at Intersections. Property lines at street intersections shall be rounded with a radius of not less than twenty (20) feet.

Cul-de-Sacs or dead-end streets shall not be greater in length than 800 1,000 feet. There shall be provided at the closed end with a turn around having an outside pavement radius of at least forty (40) feet. Frontage shall be seventy-five (75 ) feet with one hundred (100) feet width at build line.

Temporary dead-end streets shall be provided with a temporary turn around area which shall meet the requirements of this Ordinance for design, maintenance, and removal.

The distance between reverse curves shall not be less than 200 feet on a major artery or connecting routes nor less than 100 feet on any other street.

Maximum Grade. The maximum grade of a street shall not be less than six (6) percent on a major artery, twelve (12) percent on a connecting route, or fifteen (15) percent on any other street.

“Minor Subdivision” means the subdivision of land into a total of two (2) lots, parcels, tracts or building sites during a twelve (12) month period. The resultant lots must meet all of the requirements (lot size, frontage, access, etc.) of the zoning district in which they are classified. Minor subdivisions which conform to the aforementioned standards may be created on any lot, tract, or parcel which was recorded with the County Clerk of Superior Court prior to January 1* of each. calendar year provided that subject lot and all resultant lots comply with: the standards of Town Zoning and Subdivision regulations. Once any lot, tract or parcel meeting the aforementioned standards has been subdivided into a total of two lots, tracts, parcels or building sites, no further subdivision of either of the two'lots is permitted inherently for the twelve (12) month period after the land was subdivided. Any additional subdivision beyond two (2) lots per twelve (12) month period shall require consideration by the Town Council as a Use Subject to Town Council Approval.

A. Block Length. Blocks shall not be greater than 1,400 feet nor less than 600 feet in length.

B. Block Width. Blocks shall be wide enough to provide two tiers of lots of minimum depth, except where abutting upon major streets, or where other situations make this requirement impracticable in which case the Town Council may approve a single tier of lots of minimum depth.

C. Building Sites. Blocks shall be so arranged as to permit the establishment of adequate building sites that meet the lot size requirements of the Town of Clermont Land Use Ordinance.

D. General Design of Lots. All lots which shall hereafter be established in connection with the development of a Subdivision as defined by this Ordinance shall comply with the following design standards.

- 1. Street Access. Each lot hereafter established shall front or abut on a street which is to be dedicated to the public and which shall conform to the requirements of this Ordinance.

- 2. Arrangement of Lots. Side lines shall be as nearly as practical at right angles to straight street lines and radial to curved street lines.

- i. 100 feet minimum lot frontage; ii. 75 fee minimum lot frontage, and iii. 43,560 square feet (1 acre) minimum lot area.

- 2. Separate (Private) Water Supply and Individual Waste Disposal System for each Lot:

- i. 100 feet minimum width at the building line; ii. 100 feet minimum lot frontage, and iii. 43,560 square feet (1 acre) minimum lot area.

F, Additional Water and Sewer System Requirements. A “Public” water or sanitary sewer system. shall mean either a community system for a particular subdivision or a municipal or county owned system. The Hall County Health Department may require the installation of a public water or sanitary sewer system in a residential subdivision.

G. Explanation of Lot Requirements. It is the intent of these regulations to comply with and in some cases exceed State Health Laws and requirements, as stated in the Rules of the Department of Public Health, State of Georgia, for Individual Sewage Disposal Systems which, in effect, require 30,000 to 40,000 square feet area for individual water supplies and separate waste disposal systems on each lot in the type of soil found in Hall County. The regulations contained herein are designed to best serve the health and safety of the citizens of Clermont as determined by the Town Council.

H. Building Line Requirements. The front building line shall be no less than sixty-five (65) feet from the centerline of the street or no less than forty (40) feet from the right-of-way boundary, whichever is greater. Coroner lots shall observe this line on both lot frontages. Side building lines shall be no less than fifteen (15) feet from the side lot line. No above ground portion of any structure shall encroach onto or over the building lines. Developers are urged to exceed these minimum building line requirements in order to create aesthetically pleasing subdivisions. The minimum building line requirements shall be a covenant restriction, either on the plat or in a recorded covenant.
13: A. Subdivision amenities shall be subject to the conditions set forth below. The applicant shall bear the burden of providing conclusive evidence to the Planning & Zoning Advisory Committee that these conditions have been met. The Town Council may modify the conditions listed below to be more restrictive or place additional conditions which may also be more restrictive than the conditions listed below on any approval granted the applicant.
15:
If the subdivision amenities are approved, the applicant is responsible for the operation of the said amenities in conformance with these conditions. The applicant shall submit a description of the proposed amenities demonstrating that they will comply with each of the conditions listed below. Additionally, the applicant will submit a site plan showing the dimensions of the amenity site, and. showing the proposed uses with dimensions (including a realistic representation of the proposed landscaping and screening) within the site.

Conditions:

- 1. Subdivision amenities will be for the exclusive benefit of and under the control of a homeowners association whose membership includes and is limited to all lot owners of the subdivision in which the amenity site is located.

- 2. Ifthe parcel does not conform to the minimum dimensional area requirements of the zoning district in which it exists, it shall be noted on the plans submitted for approval and designated on the recorded plat as a non-buildable lot except as approved for the amenities.

- 3. No improvement (excluding parking lots) shall be located closer than fifty (50) feet from a lot line except that the Town Council may allow the setback on improvements to be reduced to twenty (20) feet when an adequate buffer is provided along the property line. Said buffer shall be a brick or stone wall or a solid wooden fence as required by the Town Council. The Town Council may permit the substitution of a vegetated buffer, to comply with the general buffer requirement. A site plan describing the details of the proposed buffer shall be submitted with the application. All buffers located near the intersection of two (2) roads or streets or the amenity site driveway and a public street shall comply with the clear vision requirements of Section 9- 3A(1) of this Ordinance. Under no circumstances may improvements (excluding parking lots) be located. closer than fifty (50) feet from a lot line when that lot line is adjacent to an arterial or collector street.

- 4. Parking lots shall be located no closer than fifty (50) feet from a lot line except that the Town Council may allow the setback to be reduced to a minimum of twelve (12) feet when an adequate buffer is provided along the property line. The buffer is to be constructed within the setback area. When the parking lot is adjacent to a road or street, the buffer shall consist of earthen berms or vegetation, to a minimum of three (3) feet. The berms will be designed so as not to cause drainage or erosion problems. When the parking

‘is adjacent to a building lot, it shall be screened by a wall or fence. The Town Council may allow the substitution of a vegetated. buffer for the wall or fence.

- 5. Facility lighting shall be of the type which prevents direct view of the light source from adjacent residences. Distance between and location of new street lights shall be approved by the Town Council.

- 6. The completed covenants for the subdivision and the documents establishing the property owners association shall be submitted for review. These documents shall include a provision that would assure maintenance of the amenity package through fees paid by the subdivision property owners association and shall provide for establishing a lien against any property failing to pay said assessment. These documents shall be submitted for approval to the Town Council. Upon approval, the documents shall be recorded simultaneously with the final plat and/or prior to the sale of any lots within the subdivision.
